newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Oct 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Oct 17.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
A parliamentary committee will visit some foreign parliaments to gather "empirical knowledge" on how to run the business of the house more effectively, government officials said.

Water Resources Minister Abdur Razzak said he was expecting soon a "satisfactory" solution to the water sharing disputes with India. The minister is scheduled to leave for New Delhi on October 28 to talk water problems with his Indian counterpart.

Former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia, now visiting Saudi Arabia, has warned her Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) "won't remain silent" if the government tried to introduce a "secular education policy".
Queen Sophia of Spain will be visiting Bangladesh during November 21-22 to see micro-credit activities of the Grameen Bank.
A bill for separation of judiciary from the executive is likely to be placed in the next session of the parliament, beginning November 1.
Bangladesh's Privatisation Board has proposed that a legal framework be made to step up the disinvestment process.
